title: Understanding the Data Model in the Agentic Security Operations Platform

blocks.text: The data model is an entity-based relational database within the Agentic Security Operations Platform (Agentic SecOps Platform). It provides the canonical schema for entities and fields across your data sources, and it defines names, types, relationships, defaults, fallback logic, and how conflicting values from multiple sources are resolved. To learn more, see About Data Model Management.
The Agentic SecOps Platform data model is focused on the following core concepts:

blocks.item: Entity-based architecture: The data model is built around entities, which offers a more meaningful, relationship-based view of security data. To learn more, see Understanding Entity Types.

Prescriptive schema: Built with specific principles and strong assumptions about how data should be structured, managed, and accessed, the data model emphasizes prescriptive structures that prioritize specific use cases within Agentic SecOps Platform applications. These data model principles are backed by Zscaler's extensive knowledge, research, and development within the security landscape.

Extensible schema: If the prescriptive schema must be adjusted, you can define your own entities, attributes, and relationships to adjust as new data sources or security tools are integrated. This extensibility is critical in keeping the data model relevant and aligned with evolving security requirements, and Zscaler recommends consulting with your Zscaler Account team to learn more.

Unified source: Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM), Asset Exposure Management (AEM), Agentic SOC, and Identity Protection use the unified and transformed data to drive effective prioritization and streamlined remediation.

blocks.heading: Processing Security Data in the Data Model

blocks.text: The following procedure shows the configuration steps necessary to process, transform, and consume data within the data model:

blocks.item: Create a data source and ingest its data. To learn more, see Creating Data Sources.

Map ingested fields to the data model. All fields within the Agentic SecOps Platform are preconfigured with field defaults, and mapping is configured per source. To learn more, see Mapping Data Sources.

Create merge and unification rules. When the rules run, the system deduplicates records across multiple sources and applies reconciliation and transformation logic using these rules. The output is a unified record. To learn more, see What Is Data Unification?, Configuring Field Unification, and Configuring Entity Unification.
View the unified records within Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM), Asset Exposure Management (AEM), Agentic SOC, and Identity Protection.

blocks.text: You can preview the data model schema for a certain entity or field on the Data Model Management page. To learn more, see Adding and Managing Entities and Fields.
The following example illustrates how two asset records are processed in the data model:

blocks.item: Two data sources report the same asset with different hostnames and operating systems.
The data model processes each source's data and associates each record field to a default Agentic SecOps Platform field.
The data model applies merge and unification rules:
Entity unification detects a duplicate and merges them into one asset.
Field unification applies reconciliation (e.g., source priority) to choose the hostname, and a transformation to normalize system OS format.
When a vulnerability is found on the asset, you see the unified asset name, hostname, and OS in the vulnerability finding.

blocks.heading: Best Practices for Configuring the Data Model

blocks.text: Consult your Zscaler Account team when making changes to the data model. Uninformed or well-meaning changes to the data model can affect data integrity and cause fragmented or duplicated data, which can result in operational inefficiencies or noncompliance.
Review the following best practices before configuring the data model:

blocks.item: Follow the established data mapping guidelines. To learn more, see Mapping Data Sources.

Start with the default configuration in the Agentic SecOps Platform, and only introduce field‑unification overrides or custom mapping transforms when business outcomes require them. To learn more, see Configuring Field Unification and Configuring Entity Unification.
Create custom entities or fields with the help of your Zscaler Account team. To learn more, see Adding and Managing Entities and Fields.
Document why an override or mapping deviation exists, and periodically review and update source mappings as vendor schemas evolve.
